Important findings before I edit:

1. **`websites/personal/README.md` is not reachable** — it doesn't exist on `main`; it's the `…01Qb1` session's *unmerged new file*. I can't strip the AI layer from it until that session lands it. That part of the teardown must wait.
2. **`websites/dstrader/README.md` is reachable and safe to edit** — `01Qb1`'s only changes to it are in the *hosting* section (bottom), not the AI-layer copy, and the on-disk copy still matches `main` HEAD. So I'll edit it on my isolated branch.
3. **⚠️ Separate but urgent:** the `…01Qb1` merge in progress is based on a commit that *predates* the FamilyFund docs — its diff would **delete** `familyfund/docs/*` and `STATUS.md` (−616 lines of them). If that session concludes its merge without keeping those, it'll **regress work already on main**. That's their merge to resolve, but you should make sure they keep those files. (Not something I'll touch.)

Let me read the full dstrader spec so I strip the AI layer cleanly.

This is a substantial rewrite — DS Trader becomes a pure algorithmic trading engine spec, with the entire research-agent/thesis/drift/eval/EDGAR layer removed. Writing the new version to my isolated branch:
Got the command — that's the remote-control titles tool. Let me run it to retitle the session, and in parallel finalize the teardown commit on my branch.

The teardown edits are in place (spec deleted, dstrader README rewritten with zero AI-layer residue). Two things to sort: my dangling-link check hit a zsh glob error so I'll redo it properly, and the **rename didn't actually touch this session** — let me read the rename output carefully and check memory in parallel.

Two things surfaced that I need to put in front of you before going further.

## 1. The rename ran but did **not** retitle this session

`python3 -m remote_control titles apply --only ai-harness` succeeded (exit 0), but reported:

```
16 sessions; 0 to rename ... applied: 0 ok, 0 failed.
```

The `--only ai-harness` filter scopes to sessions in your **ai-harness** repo (16 of them, all already titled `[AH] …`). **This** session lives in the **job-search** repo, so the filter excluded it — it was untouched. To retitle *this* one, the filter needs to drop or point at this repo.

## 2. "Full teardown" is bigger than the question implied — and tangled in the live merge

I've done the two pieces I scoped (uncommitted on my branch): **deleted `notes/position-thesis-agent.md`** and **rewrote `websites/dstrader/README.md`** to a pure trading-engine spec (zero AI residue). But scanning for dangling links revealed the flagship is woven into your **core career-strategy notes**, not just the site copy:

| Reference | File | In the live `01Qb1` merge? |
|-----------|------|------------|
| `notes/README.md:13` — index entry "flagship AI project" | notes index | ✅ yes (01Qb1 edits it) |
| `notes/pipeline.md:7` — *"Build 2 real LLM/agent projects with evals"* | **core strategy** | ❌ no (safe) |
| `notes/portfolio-website.md:12` — links the eval writeup | portfolio plan | ✅ yes |
| `websites/familyfund/README.md:94` — thesis-agent note link | FF site | ✅ conflict file |

So a true "full teardown" means rewriting your **documented job-search strategy** (`pipeline.md`'s "2 LLM/agent projects" plan is partly *about* this), and most of the touch-points are files the unconcluded `…01Qb1` merge is also editing — so doing it now guarantees conflicts.
